record.paper_title: Open problems in renewal, coupling and Palm theory
record.original_question: Let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} be a random walk on ℝ starting at 0 with i.i.d. step lengths X_1, X_2, …, and let S' = (S'_n)_{n≥0} be the version started at x ∈ ℝ. Say that the two walks admit exact coupling if they can be constructed on one probability space with an almost surely finite random time T such that S_n = S'_n for all n ≥ T. If the common step-length distribution is neither discrete nor spread out, for which starting offsets x do the two walks admit exact coupling?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 Suppose the step-lengths are neither discrete nor spread out. For what initial positions x do the random walks admit exact coupling?
Say that the random walks admit exact coupling if they can be defined on the same probability space in such a way that there is an a.s. finite random time T such that Sn = S'n for n ≥ T.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ that is neither discrete (not supported on a countable set) nor spread out (no convolution power $\mu^{*n}$ has a nontrivial absolutely continuous component with respect to Lebesgue measure). Let $X_1, X_2, \dots$ be i.i.d. random variables with common distribution $\mu$, and define the random walks
$$S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k, \qquad S'_n = x + \sum_{k=1}^n X_k', \quad n \ge 0,$$
where $(X_k')_{k\ge 1}$ is an independent copy with the same distribution $\mu$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Say that $S$ and $S'$ admit an exact coupling if there exists a probability space carrying processes $(\tilde S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ and $(\tilde S'_n)_{n\ge 0}$ with the same laws as $S$ and $S'$ respectively, and an almost surely finite random time $T$ such that $\tilde S_n = \tilde S'_n$ for all $n \ge T$.

Characterize the set of starting offsets $x \in \mathbb{R}$ for which $S$ and $S'$ admit an exact coupling.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2017 preprint (arXiv:1706.06968, "Exact Coupling of Random Walks on Polish Groups") explicitly states that it solves Thorisson's problem and provides the characterization: the random walk started at 0 admits a successful exact coupling with the version started at x if and only if there exists $n \ge 1$ with $\mu^{*n} \wedge \mu^{*n}(x + \cdot) \ne 0$ (i.e., the n-fold convolutions have a common component after shifting by x). The paper also gives convergence rates depending on the order of x.

status_evidence.title: Exact Coupling of Random Walks on Polish Groups
status_evidence.snippet: This paper solves a problem posed by H. Thorisson on successful exact coupling of random walks on R. Characterization: there exists n ≥ 1 with μ^n ∧ μ^n(x+·) ≠ 0.
status_evidence.claim: Thorisson's exact coupling problem for random walks on R was solved, with explicit characterization in terms of convolution powers of the step distribution.
